correctness.rationale: The bilinear basis identity f star g = iota(f) sigma(g) is exact. In characteristic p, the augmentation ideal J=(t-1) has J^p=0; every augmentation-zero idempotent lies in all J^(2^r), hence vanishes. On 1+J, Exp and Log are inverse additive/multiplicative group maps, valid because all terms of degree p vanish. The fixed-point equation log(f)=iota(log f)+sigma(log f) reduces through the iota +/- splitting and sigma invertibility to W. The orbit count yields dimension (p-1)/lcm(2,ord_p(2)), and exponential products yield the stated core operation. The direct verifier exhaustively checked 27, 3125, and 823543 coefficient vectors in the three prime fields, plus 729 over GF9; checks corroborate but do not replace the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The claim concerns the complete idempotent set and its induced core-quandle law for odd prime modulus at the defining characteristic. The 2020/2022 integral calculations cannot transfer by base change to characteristic p, the 2022/2023 covering and characteristic-two work has distinct hypotheses, and the 2026 commutative-quandle theorem does not apply to R_p for p>=5. A published published-finding corpus special case p=3 is excluded. The earlier signed-doubling W dimension in modular derivations is acknowledged, while the exponential bijection and resulting intrinsic quandle structure require new nonassociative-to-associative linearization. Six semantic research-record searches identified no broader covering result; unindexed literature remains a risk. Additional 2026 primary literature (arXiv:2601.07057 and arXiv:2609.09183) was inspected in full for implicit prime-modulus coverage; those results remain integral or concern different hypotheses.

value.rationale: Finite quandle-algebra idempotents and their induced quandles are motivated independently by the link-coloring enhancement of arXiv:2207.09257 Theorem 5.1. The result classifies all idempotents for infinitely many odd primes and all matching-characteristic fields, identifies the maximal nonzero idempotent family as a connected Latin core quandle, and determines an arithmetic criterion for genuinely new idempotents. It detects nontrivial high-dimensional families at p=17 and p=31, not merely a narrow recomputation. The dimension formula for the linear eigenspace alone is not counted as the contribution.
